catalyst_text: Presented positive Phase 3 results at AAD meeting
detailed_catalyst_text: One-year Phase 3 results from ICONIC-ADVANCE 1 and 2 and ICONIC-LEAD in moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis were presented at a major dermatology meeting. Data showed durable skin clearance through Week 52 with increasing PASI 100 rates, and no new safety signals; adolescent data also demonstrated sustained efficacy and favorable safety. These results reinforce durable efficacy and a favorable safety profile for an oral therapy in this indication.
catalyst_text_evidence: Protagonist Therapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ:PTGX) ("Protagonist" or "the Company") today announced new one-year Phase 3 results for ICOTYDE™ (icotrokinra) were presented at the 2026 American Academy of Dermatology (AAD) Annual Meeting. ICOTYDE demonstrated durable rates of complete skin clearance through Week 52 with no new safety signals identified. ICOTYDE also demonstrated sustained efficacy and a favorable safety profile in adolescents through Week 52.

catalyst_text: Received FDA approval for plaque psoriasis indication
detailed_catalyst_text: The FDA approved an oral IL-23 receptor antagonist for treatment of moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis in adults and adolescents 12 years and older who weigh at least 40 kg. The approval was supported by four Phase 3 studies in approximately 2,500 patients that met all primary endpoints and showed a favorable safety profile, and it triggers a $50 million milestone payment under the collaboration.
catalyst_text_evidence: Protagonist Therapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ:PTGX) ("Protagonist" or "the Company") announced 2026-03-18 that Johnson & Johnson received U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approval for ICOTYDE (icotrokinra), an interleukin-23 (IL-23) receptor antagonist for the treatment of moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis in adults and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older who weigh at least 40 kg who are candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy. ICOTYDE met all primary endpoints and demonstrated a favorable safety profile across four Phase 3 studies including 2,500 patients. FDA approval of ICOTYDE triggers a $50 million milestone payment to Protagonist.

catalyst_text: NDA accepted with priority review PDUFA in Q3
detailed_catalyst_text: The FDA accepted the NDA and granted Priority Review for an investigational therapy for adults with polycythemia vera. A PDUFA goal date was set for the third quarter of this calendar year, signaling an accelerated review timeline for a potential first-in-class treatment.
catalyst_text_evidence: Takeda and Protagonist Therapeutics, Inc. today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) accepted the New Drug Application (NDA) and granted Priority Review for rusfertide. The FDA has set a Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) goal date in the third quarter of this calendar year. Rusfertide is an investigational, first-in-class hepcidin mimetic peptide therapeutic for the treatment of adults with polycythemia vera (PV).

catalyst_text: Submitted FDA NDA for polycythemia vera treatment
detailed_catalyst_text: An NDA was submitted to the U.S. FDA seeking approval of rusfertide for adults with polycythemia vera. The filing follows positive Phase 3 VERIFY results and supports advancement into regulatory review for a potential new treatment option that may reduce phlebotomy burden and improve hematocrit control.
catalyst_text_evidence: “Takeda (…) and Protagonist Therapeutics (…) announced the submission of a New Drug Application (NDA) to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) seeking approval of rusfertide for the treatment of adults with polycythemia vera (PV).” “This NDA submission follows the positive 32-week primary analysis and 52-week results from the Phase 3 global randomized, placebo-controlled VERIFY study (NCT05210790), in which rusfertide met the primary endpoint and all four key secondary endpoints.”

catalyst_text: Announced positive Phase 3 and extension study results
detailed_catalyst_text: New 52-week results from the pivotal Phase 3 VERIFY study in polycythemia vera showed durable hematocrit control and clinical response, with 61.9% of continuously treated patients maintaining absence of phlebotomy eligibility through Week 52. A four-year analysis from the THRIVE extension reported a greater than 13-fold reduction in annual therapeutic phlebotomy rate versus baseline, reinforcing long-term benefit and a consistent safety profile.
catalyst_text_evidence: These findings further reinforce rusfertide's efficacy and safety and demonstrate durability of response, with 61.9% of patients continuously treated with rusfertide maintaining absence of phlebotomy eligibility from baseline to Week 52. Four-Year Results from the Combined REVIVE and Long-Term Extension THRIVE Study Demonstrated a 13-Fold Reduction in Annual Rate of Phlebotomies from Baseline. The results show that after transitioning to THRIVE, continued treatment with rusfertide with or without cytoreductive therapy demonstrated consistent, long-term hematocrit control with a greater than 13-fold reduction in estimated annual therapeutic phlebotomy rate compared to baseline prior to study entry in REVIVE. Prior to study entry in REVIVE, the mean annualized phlebotomy rate (i.e., phlebotomy/year) for the 46 patients who eventually rolled over to THRIVE was 9.2 phlebotomies/year. The mean annualized phlebotomy rate during THRIVE was 0.7 phlebotomies/year.

Data from Phase 2, presented at EHA, indicated that the PK-efficacy model effectively represented the plasma concentration-time profile of rusfertide as well as the progression of Hb, as noted on June 9, 2023.
Preclinical findings provided evidence of proof-of-concept in models of skin inflammation and colitis, as reported on May 12, 2023.
Data from Phase 2 indicated that in all 16 patients with erythrocytotic PV, rusfertide showed a swift decrease in hematocrit to below 45% within a few weeks, as reported on December 12, 2021.

Data from Phase 2 was published on November 15, 2021. The Phase 2 trial achieved its main goal, showing that patients treated with rusfertide experienced 0.009 phlebotomies per month throughout the study, in contrast to 0.28 phlebotomies per month prior to the treatment.
As of November 3, 2021, the Phase 2 trial and the development of the candidate have been halted.
The clinical hold for Phase 2 was removed on October 11, 2021.

The Phase 2b trial was halted after an interim analysis on March 26, 2018. Nevertheless, the company indicated on August 6, 2018, that a mistake made by the CRO played a role in this outcome. A meeting with the FDA is planned for the second half of the year to discuss further developments.
